articles.title: Groupby Collects Adjacent Runs and Shares Its Input Iterator

articles.body: A list of labels can contain the same value in more than one place. A run-based summary asks where equal labels appear consecutively. A per-label summary asks how many or which items share a label across the entire input. Those are different questions. The Python groupby reference defines consecutive grouping and explains that the yielded groups share their source. The example materializes each run before advancing when it needs to retain that run. Keep a run separate from a global category The first fixture places A on both sides of B. Another deliberately sorts those labels, changing their order and therefore changing the grouping problem. A third advances the outer iterator before consuming the earlier group.

articles.title: Don't miss Saturn shine close to the moon on Nov. 20
articles.excerpt: The moon shines with Saturn in the constellation Pisces after sunset on Nov. 20
articles.body: The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

articles.body: Five datasets, totally different formats. Five different answers to one simple question: what is one row? SWE-smith: a task with a bug put in it. SWE-Gym: a task. ToolACE: a made up dialogue. CommitPackFT: a before and after pair, no process at all. MegaBit-trajctories(mine): one full session that actually ran. Put those in one table the lazy way and every number after is a lie . So I built a method to compare things that share almost nothing. It is all CPU. No GPU, no training, no weeks. One script and an afternoon. Here it is, step by step, so you can use it on anything. Step 1: Fix the unit before any number Row zero is not a number. It is a question: what is one row? articles.title: Surprising No One, GTA 6's Comedy Is All Over the Place
articles.excerpt: GTA 6 is the latest Grand Theft Auto to continue Rockstar's pedigree of satirizing literally everyone across the whole political spectrum. Yay...
articles.body: More than being deviously fun crime sandboxes, every Grand Theft Auto game also acts as a snapshot of American culture at the time of its release. These games have never pulled any punches, taking swings at everything from the paparazzi to politics to the most innocuous corners of pop culture. GTA 6 was sure to take the same shots, but at a time when the targets are moving faster than ever. Could a game that has been in the works for more than a decade possibly have humor that felt up to date? Would it be careful to punch up rather than turn the country’s most vulnerable people into punchlines? And would it have the stones to take on President Donald Trump, a man who has dominated America’s political culture throughout the game’s entire development cycle?

articles.title: Fitbit Edge owners are complaining about the lack of hourly movement reminders
articles.excerpt: Fitbit Edge tracks your hourly steps, but it won't remind you to take them.
articles.body: TL;DR Fitbit Edge owners report that the tracker lacks hourly reminders to move. The tracker still monitors hourly activity but doesn’t vibrate to remind users to reach their 250-step goal. Reminders to move have been available on Fitbit devices since 2016, helping users stay active throughout the day. One of the simplest ways Fitbit has helped people stay active over the years is by encouraging them to get out of their chairs. As far back as the original Fitbit Alta in 2016, Fitbit offered reminders to move. Rather than letting you cram all your daily steps into an evening walk, the feature encouraged you to spread your activity throughout the day. However, those upgrading to the new Google Fitbit Edge are discovering that their wrists have gone unusually quiet.

articles.body: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters.

articles.title: ChatGPT can transcribe as you speak now with Live Dictation
articles.excerpt: ChatGPT can receive audio prompts from your microphone faster now with a Live Dictation feature that transcribes as you speak, rather than waiting until you finish recording. It's rolling out now glob…
articles.body: ChatGPT can receive audio prompts from your microphone faster now with a Live Dictation feature that transcribes as you speak, rather than waiting until you finish recording. It's rolling out now globally on all ChatGPT plans on the web, desktop app, and iOS and Android apps. While using dictation in ChatGPT, you can tap or click the audio waveform to show the live text transcript the AI is generating, then edit it in the prompt box when you're done. Dictation in ChatGPT is getting faster and more reliable. With Live Dictation, your speech turns into text as you talk, so you spend less time waiting for your message to finish transcribing. … Read the full story at The Verge.

articles.title: Empire State Building glows gold for NASA's Voyager spacecraft | Space photo of the day for Nov. 19, 2026
articles.excerpt: The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth.
articles.body: The Empire State Building is illuminated in gold to celebrate Voyager 1 hitting one light-day from Earth, seen here on Tuesday, Nov. 17, 2026, from SUMMIT One Vanderbilt in New York City. (Image credit: NASA/Bill Ingalls) The Empire State Building glowed in glittering gold last night (Nov. 17) to celebrate NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hitting one light-day from Earth. And it isn't the only building celebrating this achievement with a sparkling display. What is it? Today (Nov. 18) at 5:16 a.m. EST (1016 GMT), NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft hit one light-day from Earth. About 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers) away, this is the point at which it takes a full day (or 24 hours) for one light particle to get from us to the probe.
